lead: Florida rarely needs heat, but kitchen, electrical and wildfire risks are real. SootMend helps homes and businesses from Miami to Jacksonville and Tampa recover from fire, smoke and soot.
risk: kitchen and electrical fires, wildfires in pine and palmetto, and soot damage in humid air
why: Nearly nine in ten Florida homes heat with electricity, and many need heat only a few days a year. Most fire damage starts with cooking, dryers, electrical problems and, more recently, lithium-ion batteries in e-bikes and scooters. Condo towers and apartments let smoke spread through halls and floors.

Florida also has a real wildfire season, usually peaking in late winter and spring. Pine flatwoods and palmetto burn hot, and FEMA approved fire assistance in 2026 during a dry spring. In the humid climate, soot and smoke residue absorb moisture and stain fast.
problems: Miami, Fort Lauderdale, Tampa and Orlando
tips: Clean dryer lint traps and vents often.
Charge e-bike and scooter batteries away from exits and never overnight.
Clear pine needles and palmetto near the house in spring.
Run AC or dehumidifiers after a fire to slow soot staining.
insurance: Many Floridians are insured through Citizens Property Insurance, the state-created insurer of last resort, so check whether your policy is with Citizens or a private carrier.
areas: Jacksonville, Miami, Tampa, Orlando, St. Petersburg, Tallahassee, Fort Myers and the Panhandle are all covered.

faq.q: Why does soot stain faster in Florida?
faq.a: High humidity lets soot absorb moisture, which helps acids and oils set into paint, grout and fabric. Running AC or dehumidifiers and starting cleanup within days limits permanent staining.
